subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: Should an explicit `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` fail startup after a bounded readiness period when no Tailnet address exists, or remain available locally through the current loopback degradation?
rationale: Both outcomes are defensible but materially different: fail-closed preserves explicit operator intent while risking availability during Tailscale boot races, whereas loopback degradation is network-safe but silently removes the configured remote endpoint.

options.title: Wait, then fail closed
options.body: Wait briefly for a Tailnet address, then exit clearly and nonzero rather than starting a loopback-only gateway.

options.title: Keep safe degradation
options.body: Retain loopback fallback but emit a prominent startup warning and health/status signal that Tailnet reachability is unavailable.

options.title: Add an explicit fallback policy
options.body: Introduce a configuration choice between strict Tailnet startup and loopback degradation, accepting additional configuration and upgrade surface.

recommendation.title: Wait, then fail closed
recommendation.body: Wait briefly for a Tailnet address, then exit clearly and nonzero rather than starting a loopback-only gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision affects gateway startup policy and compatibility, and this person has the strongest recent gateway history and is subscribed to the issue.
